subject: Agriculture
title: Food Miles Myth
description: A fast breakdown of Food Miles Myth for builders.

hook.text: Eating local sounds green. But a tomato shipped from Spain may have a smaller carbon footprint than one grown in a UK greenhouse.

buildup.text: Food miles measure distance, not emissions. Growing food matters more than moving it.

discovery.text: A ship carrying 10,000 tons of grain emits less CO₂ per kilogram-mile than a car carrying groceries from the store.

twist.text: Lamb from New Zealand shipped to the UK has a lower footprint than UK-raised lamb because NZ grass-feeds year-round.

climax.text: What you eat—especially beef vs. plants—dwarfs where it comes from in environmental impact.

punchline.text: Eat less meat to help the planet. Eat local for other reasons—but not carbon.

quiz.question: Why can food shipped long distances sometimes have a lower carbon footprint?
options: Production methods matter more than transport, which is only 6% of food emissions
